page: Amazon Web Services c6i.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz with 4 vCPUs, which map to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average range. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with Passmark memory scores and uncached read/write speeds registering in the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Cryptographic and single-threaded compression tasks perform moderately well, utilizing hardware flags like AVX-512 and AES.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6i.xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile suitable for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local storage. Given the weak multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, it is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, and basic utility applications rather than heavy database operations or intensive multi-threaded compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides dedicated CPU allocation but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 2 Gbps baseline network. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, supported by AVX-512 and cryptography hardware acceleration, alongside average performance in static web serving and single-threaded compression. However, multi-core processing and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% of tested systems. Consequently, the c6i.xlarge is qualitatively cost-effective for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic utility workloads, but is less suited for memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized applications.
